summary: 100-foot Wisconsin standard tower in Lincoln County west of Tomahawk, built December 1939 per the register; a July 1977 burglary report names a state DNR employee as the reporter. Listed as standing.

facts.design: Wisconsin standard tower with an external protected ladder

events.note: July 1977 burglary reported by a state DNR employee; door torn off, glass broken, communications radio damaged
Registered June 19, 2017; nominated by Tyler Bormann

evidence.supports: 100-foot Wisconsin standard tower with external protected ladder, built December 1939
evidence.quote: This 100-foot Wisconsin standard tower features an external protected ladder. It was built in December 1939.

evidence.supports: administered by the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources

evidence.quote: A burglary at the Zenith fire tower west of Tomahawk off Highway 86 was reported by a state Department of Natural Resources employe last Sunday.

evidence.supports: door torn off, glass broken, communications radio damaged
evidence.quote: the door was torn off its hinges, glass was broken, and a communications radio damaged.

evidence.supports: 2015 AP report: dozens of Wisconsin towers from the 1930s and 1940s being taken out of commission
evidence.quote: Dozens of towers built mainly in the 1930s and 1940s for spotting forest fires in Wisconsin are being taken out of commission.

evidence.supports: 2015 date (copyright year printed on the AP text)

notes_for_editor: Build date and height rest on the register alone; no second source for the 1939 date was found. Staffing, access, and rental are not covered by any source checked. The 1977 item is quoted on Central US Lookouts; its newspaper name is printed as Wausaw on that page, so the paper is not named in the story. A 1940 Wisconsin Historical Society photo of a Tomahawk forest protection headquarters came up in search, but it does not mention the lookout, so it was not used. A USDA Forest Service PDF named in a search snippet returned 404 and was not used.
